title: Igor Girkin

fields.label: Position held
fields.value: Minister of Defence of the Donetsk People's Republic

summary: Igor Vsevolodovich Girkin, also known as Igor Ivanovich Strelkov, is a Russian military veteran and former Federal Security Service officer who played a significant role in the Russian annexation of Crimea and the subsequent conflict in eastern Ukraine, particularly in the [[donbas|Donbas]] region. His actions have led to multiple international sanctions and a life sentence in absentia for his involvement in the downing of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17.

sections.heading: Early Life
paragraphs: Igor Girkin was born in Moscow, Russia, on 17 December 1970. He developed a strong ideological stance during his time at the Moscow State Institute for History and Archives, where he was particularly interested in military history and advocated for a return to monarchism.

In the 1990s, Girkin contributed to the right-wing newspaper Zavtra, which was associated with anti-Semitic nationalist Alexander Prokhanov. He covered various military conflicts, including the Russian war against separatists in Chechnya and Dagestan.

sections.heading: FSB Service
paragraphs: Girkin served in the Russian Federal Security Service (FSB) from 1996 until his retirement in 2013, including participation in counter-terrorism operations in Chechnya. His military background includes involvement in conflicts in Moldova's breakaway region of Transnistria and the Bosnian War.
He has been linked to human rights abuses during the Chechen Wars, with allegations of forced disappearances and murders of civilians in Chechnya.

sections.heading: Annexation of Crimea and Donbas War
paragraphs: Following the [[ukrainian-war-of-independence|Ukrainian revolution]] in February 2014, Girkin played a pivotal role in the [[russian-annexation-of-crimea|annexation of Crimea]]. He was invited to [[crimea|Crimea]] by local pro-Russian politicians to serve as a security advisor, where he coordinated militias and was involved in the occupation of key government buildings.

On 12 April 2014, Girkin led armed militants in the capture of Sloviansk, which marked the beginning of the [[war-in-donbas|Donbas War]]. His actions in this conflict led to his appointment as Minister of Defense in the self-proclaimed [[donetsk-peoples-republic|Donetsk People's Republic]], a position from which he was later dismissed after the downing of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17.

sections.heading: Legal Consequences and Recent Developments
paragraphs: Girkin was charged with terrorism by [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] authorities and sanctioned by multiple countries due to his prominent role in the conflict. He received a life sentence in absentia in the Netherlands for his involvement in the downing of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17, which resulted in the deaths of 298 civilians.

In 2024, Girkin was convicted of inciting extremism in Russia and sentenced to four years in prison. His political activism has continued, with a focus on criticizing the Russian military and advocating for a more aggressive approach in [[ukraine|Ukraine]].
